ModMetadata.Name: Terraforming Reloaded
ModMetadata.Author: XCeled
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]Terraform the planet[/h1] The air outside is no longer bottomless. What you vent stays. What your base draws in is gone. Move enough of the right gases and the pressure, temperature, sky and weather outside change for good, saved with your world.
[b]Release candidate.[/b] Every part of this is checked against the game by automated runs, but nobody has played a world all the way through on it yet. You are the first. Back up your save, and report anything odd on GitHub with your Player.log.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Two things set the temperature[/h2] [b]Which gas it is.[/b] Each one either traps heat or sheds it: [table] [tr][th]Effect[/th][th]Gases[/th][/tr] [tr][td][b]Traps heat[/b][/td][td]pollutant (strongest), volatiles, carbon dioxide, steam[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Sheds heat[/b][/td][td]nitrous oxide (strongest), hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Does neither[/b][/td][td]helium, hydrazine, hydrochloric acid, ozone, silanol[/td][/tr] [/table] Nitrogen and oxygen are not filler. Both shed heat, and harder the thicker they get, which is why a breathable mix still wants carbon dioxide alongside it.
[b]How much of it there is.[/b] Thick air narrows the gap between day and night whatever it is made of. Helium is the clean example: it neither traps nor sheds, so it is pure thickening.
[hr][/hr] [h2]How it plays[/h2] [list] [*]An endgame project for a base built to move gas in bulk: rockets hauling ice back from orbit, gas traders, big vents, tank farms. [*]Hot worlds are hot because of the air they start with. Strip the greenhouse gases out of Venus or Vulcan and they cool. [*]Cold worlds warm in stages. Vent a gas that freezes at the temperature you have now and it just snows into the ice caps, doing nothing. So you start with a gas that stays airborne while it is still that cold, let it lift the planet a little, and that unlocks the next gas up. Everything that froze on the way is still there, and the caps hand it back as the planet warms. [*]The Moon and Mimas start with nothing. Their first air swings hard between day and night until it thickens. [*]Storms are milder on a world you have cooled. [*]A world you have not touched reads exactly as it does without the mod. [*]Custom worlds work. WORLDS.md in the mod folder is for world authors. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]How long it takes[/h2] One setting: [b]Planet size[/b]. [table] [tr][th]Size[/th][th]Roughly[/th][/tr] [tr][td][b]Short[/b][/td][td]17 hours[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Standard[/b][/td][td]85 hours[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Long[/b][/td][td]410 hours[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Shipped[/b], the game's real planet[/td][td]1,650 hours[/td][/tr] [/table] [b]Treat these as rough scale, not a promise.[/b] They are calculated from how much gas a large, heavily automated base can move in an hour, not measured from a real playthrough, because nobody has finished one yet. A smaller or more hands-on base will take considerably longer.
Hours are for making Mars breathable, meaning you can stand outside with your helmet off. The Moon is similar, Venus and Vulcan roughly three times longer, Mimas six, Europa nine. Size changes nothing else. A save made before you installed the mod carries the full-size planet until you rescale it.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Console (F3)[/h2] [list] [*][b]terraform[/b] : pressure, temperature, gases, and whether the mod is running [*][b]terraform size <share> confirm[/b] : rescale the planet you are on without touching its air [*][b]terraform reset confirm[/b] : put the planet back as the world ships. Your base is untouched [*][b]terraform curves export[/b] / [b]reload[/b] : tune the temperature response. See CURVES.md [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]Removing it[/h2] Your changed planet lives in the save, so deleting the mod does not undo it. Run [b]terraform reset confirm[/b], save, quit, then disable. Skip that and a changed world snaps back to its shipped temperature: a breathable Venus is 737 K again, and new air on the Moon sits near absolute zero.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Good to know[/h2] [list] [*]Settings are in the StationeersLaunchPad config editor and apply at once, except those marked as needing a restart. [*]The pressure ceiling deletes air permanently. Leave it at 0 unless you mean it. [*]Multiplayer: the host needs the mod. Clients without it can still join. Untested. [*]Tutorials are left alone. [*]If a game update changes what this depends on, the mod switches itself off and says why in the log rather than risk your save. [*]The devs appear to be working on this framework themselves, so an update could break this mod or make it obsolete. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [b]Requires[/b] [url=https://github.com/StationeersLaunchPad/StationeersLaunchPad]StationeersLaunchPad[/url]
